extracted.intended_audience: writers and readers of science fiction & fantasy short fiction; potential contributors and subscribers to Lightspeed Magazine
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the kinds of fiction and nonfiction content Lightspeed publishes (genre ranges, formats, and editorial orientation), plus publication frequency and formats for readers/subscribers. Useful for authors deciding whether their short stories/novelettes or nonfiction pieces fit the magazine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted genres (science fiction and fantasy)
rubrics_metrics.description: In its pages, you will find science fiction: from near-future, sociological soft SF, to far-future, star-spanning hard SF—and fantasy: from epic fantasy, sword-and-sorcery, and contemporary urban tales, to magical realism, science-fantasy, and folktales.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lightspeed publishes a wide range across both SF and fantasy subgenres; submissions should fit somewhere within these described subgenres and tonal ranges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiction formats and issue composition
rubrics_metrics.description: In each issue, you will find eight pieces of short fiction (a mix of short stories and novelettes) from a variety of authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The magazine's fiction slots are short stories and novelettes; authors should target those formats and be aware competition is for one of roughly eight fiction slots per issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonfiction feature types
rubrics_metrics.description: Lightspeed also offers a variety of nonfiction features, including feature interviews, Q&As with our authors that go behind-the-scenes of their stories, book and media reviews, and more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonfiction submissions should fall into those kinds of features (interviews, behind-the-scenes Q&As, reviews, etc.) rather than being general essays outside those categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication frequency and distribution formats
rubrics_metrics.description: You can read Lightspeed for free online, or you can read and subscribe to our ebook editions. Our ebook issues publish on the first of every month and are available for sale via our ebookstore (in Mobi, ePub, and PDF format) and are also available in other formats such as Kindle and Nook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and readers should expect monthly ebook issues in multiple digital formats; subscription options and distribution channels are explicitly supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscription benefits and volume
rubrics_metrics.description: A 12 month subscription to Lightspeed includes more than 100 stories (around 700,000 words of fiction). Subscribing to Lightspeed saves you $1 off the cover price of each issue (savings of 25% on each issue).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes the annual volume of fiction and the economic benefit of subscribing; useful for contributors to understand the magazine's output and readership value proposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial orientation / mission
rubrics_metrics.description: Sign-up for a subscription now and you’ll see where science fiction and fantasy comes from, where it is now, and where it’s going.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lightspeed positions itself as a venue interested in the history, current state, and future directions of SF/F; submissions that engage with emerging trends or the evolution of the genres may align well with editorial goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track record / quality indication (awards and nominations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Launched in 2010, Lightspeed is a two-time winner of the Hugo Award, and stories from the magazine have been nominated for major genre awards dozens of times, including the Hugo Award, the Nebula Award, the World Fantasy Award, and the Theodore Sturgeon Award. Our editor, John Joseph Adams, has been nominated for the Hugo Award twelve times and the World Fantasy Award eight times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list of awards and nominations signals a high editorial standard and history of publishing award-caliber work; prospective contributors can infer competitive quality expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Range of authors published
rubrics_metrics.description: In each issue, you will find ... a mix of short stories and novelettes from a variety of authors—from the bestsellers and award-winners you already know to the best new voices you haven’t heard of yet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lightspeed publishes both established and emerging writers; new voices are considered alongside well-known authors, indicating openness to debut or lesser-known contributors if the work fits.
